about: Harder draw-language A/B questions over the shopfront fixture, to separate arms that all ground the easy set. Every question needs a 5+ hop chain, a fan-out to 3+ backends, or two flows that meet; several invite a plausible shortcut the scan does NOT have (noted per question in trap). Every expectPath hop is a real, same-direction scan edge; the driver re-checks that. focus starts with "repo" so the slice is the whole 36-node repo at --max-nodes 36: the repo's edgeless focus pulls in its services and stores, and the breadth-first walk reaches every file.

questions.question: Starting at the gateway's entry file, draw every way a request can end up at the Stripe code in the payments service. Show each file it passes through.
questions.trap: orders/app/routes.py -> payments/src/index.js (skipping payments_client.py) is not a scan edge

questions.question: Draw every backend file the gateway's entry file reaches through its route files, and which route files use the gateway's shared HTTP helper.
questions.trap: gateway/src/routes/payments.ts -> gateway/src/lib/http.ts is not a scan edge (the other three routes import it)

questions.kind: 4-hop chain + topic shared by two services
questions.question: How does a customer get notified after placing an order through the gateway? Draw from the gateway's entry file to the notifications worker, with arrows in the direction the scan records them.
questions.trap: orders/app/events.py -> notifications/worker.py is not a scan edge, and neither is order.created -> notifications/worker.py (the worker's edge points at the topic)

questions.kind: two flows joining at a store
questions.question: An invoice request comes in at the edge proxy. Draw how it reaches invoice data, and how the invoice service's payment calls reach stored payments. Show where the two flows meet.
questions.trap: InvoiceController.java -> PaymentClient.java is not a scan edge; the controller and the payment client are not linked

questions.question: Which services share the postgres database? For each one, draw the path from that service's entry file to postgres. Leave out services that never touch it.
questions.trap: inventory/server.py -> postgres and payments/src/stripe.js -> postgres are not scan edges

questions.question: The shipping service is reached two ways: a gateway request and the order.created event. Draw both, the request all the way to where the shipment is stored and the event from the orders code that publishes it.
questions.trap: shipping/subscriber.go -> shipping/main.go is not a scan edge (the subscriber does not hand off to main.go), and order.created -> subscriber.go is backwards

questions.question: Starting at the orders service's main file, draw every backend it reaches (other services, stores and topics), following each branch to its end.
questions.trap: inventory/server.py -> postgres and orders/app/routes.py -> orders/app/models.py are not scan edges
